conviction_note: The main finding goes against the guide. The FY26 revenue guide of $775-800M was explicitly conditioned on 'category price levels remain stabilized at current levels' (Aug 6 deck). USDA's Oct 30 report shows national loose large white at $0.35/dz, breaking stock at $0.08/dz and NY cartoned at $0.72/dz, while pastured and free-range eggs are the most promoted type at retail. So the condition behind the guide has failed, and an EBITDA guide cut is the likely swing. This is partly priced: Street FY revenue averages $763.8M with a high of $774.9M, below the guide low, puts are bid at +4.0 vol points, and the stock is 76% off its high. It is opposed by a crowded short (25.7% of float, 4.55 days to cover) that has squeezed this name +16-18% before. Net: a mild negative lean, p_up 45, on a large unsigned move of 15%. The findings sum to -1.2 against a scaled -1.5, and the two agree in sign.
bar: DISPUTED, so findings that depend on the bar are capped small. Q3 revenue: $182.3M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VITL/earnings-forecasts) against $199.8M (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/VITL). The sweep's aggregator figure of ~$182M probably comes from the same family as Benzinga's. Q3 adjusted EPS: -$0.10 (Benzinga), -$0.13 (Earnings Whispers), ~-$0.14 (sweep aggregator). FY2026 revenue consensus: $763.8M average, $748.2-774.9M range, 10 analysts, FY adj EPS -$0.38 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/vitl/forecast/, read 2026-11-02). The company guide is sourced: FY26 net revenue $775-800M, adjusted EBITDA $0-10M (including a mid-$30M oversupply cost), capex $70-75M, reaffirmed 2026-08-06 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579733/000119312526336692/vitl-ex99_1.htm). The company also said it expects 'sequential improvement in net revenue and adjusted EBITDA in Q3' from Q2's $166.0M / -$26.6M. H1 revenue was $353.2M, so the guide needs $422-447M in H2. Street FY is about $411M for H2, meaning the Street already sits below the revenue guide. Street FY EPS of -$0.38 against H1 adj EPS of about -$0.50 implies positive adjusted EPS in H2, concentrated in Q4. I sized against $182.3M.
positioning_check: Short interest: 8.89M shares, 25.68% of float, 20.70% of shares outstanding, 4.55 days to cover; prior month 8.69M, so it is still building (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/vitl/statistics/, checked 2026-11-02; settlement date not shown). Other sources range from 20.4% to 29.1% of float (Equibles as of 2026-08-20; Benzinga mid-October). This is a crowded short. Options: 25-delta skew +4.02 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 1.17, event-implied move 16.0% (straddle 20.1% to the Nov 20 expiry), but the ATM spread is 46% of mid, so the figure is indicative only. Tape: spot $8.83, -4.5% over 20 days, -76.4% from the 52-week high, +8.2% above the 52-week low. In October analysts cut targets to or below spot (TD Cowen $11 to $8 on Oct 13, Stifel $11 to $9 on Oct 15). BlackRock's 13G/A of 2026-10-27 shows 2.57M shares, about 6% of outstanding, down from the 12.1% reported in January 2026.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide was explicitly conditioned on 'category price levels remain stabilized at current levels' (Aug 6 deck, slide 18). That deck's USDA wholesale chart had large white near ~$1.45/dz and rising at week 31. USDA's Egg Markets Overview of Oct 30, 2026 shows national loose large white at $0.35/dz, NY cartoned formula at $0.72/dz and breaking stock at $0.08/dz. VITL sells its excess eggs into the breaker channel, which cost it $19.5M of gross profit in Q2, and a lower conventional price widens its retail price gap. The stated condition for the guide has therefore failed. Revenue consensus ($763.8M) is already below the guide low ($775M), but the Street's FY EPS (-$0.38, implying positive H2 EPS concentrated in Q4) still sits inside the $0-10M EBITDA guide. The exposed number is a cut to the EBITDA or Q4 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line is what has moved this stock. The Q1 2026 print with a sharp FY cut went -20.67% (2026-05-07). Q4 2025 (2026-02-26), with a weak guide, went -10.81%. Q2 2026, with the guide reaffirmed, went only +2.21% (2026-08-06). Guide raises in 2025 went +17.59% and +16.13%.
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue half is priced: every Street FY revenue estimate sits below the guide low. The EBITDA half is not visibly priced. If the Street had marked Q4 to $0.35 eggs and $0.08 breaker stock, FY EPS consensus would be at or below H1's -$0.50 rather than at -$0.38, and targets would not average $12.22. Against that, the skew is +4 vol points and the stock is 8% above its low, so some of this sits in the price.
findings.independence: The company's own guide condition and the Aug wholesale chart are in https://s205.q4cdn.com/845857233/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/v2/Q2-2026-Earnings-Presentation-MASTER-UPDATED.pdf (slides 5 and 18). Trading Economics' egg series shows -23% over the month and -78% over the year as of 2026-11-02 (https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/eggs-us). This is a proxy for magnitude: the company has not said how much it is exposed. It shares the USDA document with the next finding.

findings.finding: Competitive promotion inside VITL's own tier: USDA's Oct 30 report says 'non-organic free-range and pastured shell eggs continue to be the highest featured among the retail chains'. Pastured brown eggs were featured in 4,236 stores at an average ad price of $5.59/dz and free-range brown in 1,951 stores at $4.61. VITL's own Q2 ARP was $8.16 per EQ unit. The FY guide also assumes 'competitive activity does not intensify further' (Q2 release), and VITL launched its own sub-$5 free-range pilot at Target on Oct 23. Both point to continued pressure on price gaps and price/mix into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Widening price gaps and competitor promotions were the stated cause of the Q1 2026 miss and cut (-20.67%). The Q2 narrowing of the price gaps came with the guide reaffirmed (+2.21%).
findings.why_not_priced: USDA feature-activity tables are not on the sell-side wire. If this were priced, previews would be framing the Q4 price/mix risk rather than the Q3 sequential improvement. The analyst target cuts to $8-9 in mid-October may partly reflect it.
findings.independence: Same USDA document as the finding above, so it counts as a related reading. The company's own free-range pilot under $5 (https://s205.q4cdn.com/845857233/files/doc_news/Vital-Farms-Introduces-a-Higher-Standard-for-Free-Range-Eggs-Through-Limited-Pilot-at-Select-Target-Retail-Stores-2026.pdf, 2026-10-23) independently shows the company moving down the price ladder.

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Cal-Maine's quarter ended Aug 29, 2026 (reported Sep 30) shows specialty shell egg sales -14.0%, with average selling price per dozen -10.7% and volume -3.8%. Specialty segment operating profit fell to $14.9M from $64.2M. Management still called specialty demand 'constructive'. This covers two of the three months of VITL's Q3 and points to continued price/mix deflation in specialty eggs. Q2 VITL revenue was -10.1% YoY; the $182.3M Q3 bar requires sequential growth of about 10% from $166.0M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pure revenue surprises have moved VITL less than guidance. Q2 2026 beat its revenue estimate ($166.0M against ~$160-170M, depending on source) and went +2.21%.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer reported after VITL last spoke (Aug 6), and VITL's Q3 revenue consensus has not visibly moved. That conclusion is weak because the bar is disputed ($182.3M against $199.8M). If the peer read were priced, the $199.8M figure would have disappeared from aggregators.
findings.independence: The Benzinga transcript summary of the Cal-Maine call (https://www.benzinga.com/news/26/09/62080696) repeats the same numbers, so it is the same source family. This is a proxy: Cal-Maine specialty includes cage-free and brown eggs, not only pastured.

findings.finding: VITL's own Circana data, re-published in its September 2026 investor deck, shows Q3 entering with momentum. Average weekly volume per store selling per item was 27 in the 4 weeks to 7/19, the highest since February and +12.5% from April. At a top-10 retailer the price gap fell to $0.27 from $1.79, with velocity +27% and new households +27.2%. The deck reaffirms full-year TDPs of 150-160 and a Q4 average of 170-175, against 148.7 year to date through Q2. That supports Q3 revenue clearing the $182.3M bar on volume, even with price deflation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came with a revenue beat and these same velocity slides and went +2.21%. This name has not paid much for revenue beats when the guide was not raised.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are company slides first shown Aug 6. What is not public is August-September scanner data. If the market believed the slides, the stock would not have fallen from ~$12.36 after Q2 to $8.83.
findings.independence: Management said on the Q2 call that distribution gains 'will become visible in scanner data throughout the third quarter' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579733/000119312526336692/vitl-ex99_1.htm). That is company-sourced; I found no independent scanner readout for Aug-Sep.

findings.finding: Crowded short into a reset bar: 8.89M shares short, 25.68% of float and 4.55 days to cover, up from 8.69M the prior month. The stock is 76% off its high and 8% above its 52-week low, and in October analysts cut targets to or below spot (TD Cowen $8, Stifel $9). Any reassurance on Q4 or the EBITDA guide has a squeeze mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two prints with positive guidance surprises went +17.59% and +16.13% (2025). Even a bare reaffirmation on a beaten-down tape held at +2.21% (2026-08-06).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is itself the market's position, so this is the counterweight to the negative findings rather than an unpriced fact. It would be absent if shorts had covered into the print, and short interest was still rising last month.
findings.independence: Equibles reported ~20.4% of float with 6.1 days to cover as of 2026-08-20 (https://equibles.com/stocks/VITL), so the crowding predates October. The analyst target data comes from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/vitl/forecast/.

findings.finding: Street estimates were reset lower in the four weeks before the print: TD Cowen (Moskow) cut its target from $11 to $8 on Oct 13 with a Hold, below the then-spot of ~$8.89. Stifel cut from $11 to $9 on Oct 15, and DA Davidson cut again on Oct 27, citing execution risk. A target below spot from a Hold-rated analyst suggests the estimate cuts are about fundamentals (likely scanner data), not only valuation.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-print target cuts preceded both the -20.67% (May) and the +2.21% (Aug) prints, so they have no consistent signal on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: These are on the wire and largely priced: the stock fell 3-5% on the TD Cowen day (https://www.webull.com/news/15747808187343872, 10/14). The residual is that the reasoning behind a sub-spot target was not published.
findings.independence: The DA Davidson cut of Oct 27 appears in the Investing.com headline list at https://www.rava.com/noticias?ticker=VITL_US. The amount was not given.

findings.finding: Financing, and what it buys: Q2 cash was $21.2M with $30.0M of debt, H1 operating cash flow was -$45.9M, and H1 capex was $37.5M against a $70-75M FY guide. In August the company replaced its revolver with a $125M 3-year term loan and a $60M ABL, and terminated the buyback (Aug 3). The money funds capex already being slowed (VXR and accelerator farms) and operating losses, not a demand ramp: volume is declining. I found no covenant-pressure or going-concern language. The Q3 10-Q will show how much of the term loan was drawn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The facility was announced with Q2 (+2.21%). The market did not treat it as distress.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The residual is Q3 cash burn: with Q3 EBITDA expected near breakeven and capex of about $15-18M, net debt rises again. That would only matter if paired with an EBITDA guide cut.
findings.independence: The Aug 6 8-K carries items 1.01, 1.02 and 2.03 (EDGAR submissions, https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001579733.json). Same company document family.

findings.finding: The farm network quietly shrank: the Aug 6 deck said '625+ small farms, 10M+ birds'. The Oct 14 campaign release says 'more than 600' and the Oct 23 release says 'works with 600 small farms'. That is consistent with the farmer contract amendments and supply right-sizing management described. Less supply means fewer eggs dumped into the $0.08/dz breaker channel, which supports gross margin against the oversupply cost that hit Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line specifically. Margin recovery commentary at Q2 (+2.21%) was received tepidly.
findings.why_not_priced: A boilerplate change in a press-release footer is not something aggregators track. If it were priced, analysts would be modelling lower Q4 breaker losses, which the target cuts do not suggest.
findings.independence: The Behind Every Carton release of 2026-10-14 says 'more than 600 real family farms' (https://finviz.com/news/402539/vital-farms-launches-the-behind-every-carton-campaign-to-show-consumers-the-real-farms-and-farmers-who-produce-the-good-eggs-every-day). The Aug figure is in the Sep deck (https://s205.q4cdn.com/845857233/files/content_files/2026/Sep/Investor-Presentation-Short-September-2026.pdf, slide 5). All company sources; boilerplate rounding is a real alternative explanation.

findings.finding: Defensive governance: on Aug 11, 2026 the board adopted amended bylaws that expand advance-notice disclosure for stockholder nominations and proposals, add director-candidate eligibility standards and add emergency bylaws (8-K filed Aug 17, 8-K/A to add the Item 5.03 label). Boards usually do this when they anticipate a nomination fight or an approach. Combined with a stock down ~75%, an activist or a strategic announcement at the print is possible but not evidenced. No 13D has been filed since July.
findings.why_not_priced: A bylaw 8-K with no press release goes unread. If an approach were priced, the stock would not be trading 8% above its 52-week low with puts bid.
findings.independence: There is an unverified aggregator snippet about 'strategic options including take-private' surfacing on 2026-09-16 (listed in rejected_candidates). No primary confirmation.

findings.finding: Passive holder exit: BlackRock's Schedule 13G/A of 2026-10-27 reports voting power over 2.57M shares, about 6% of 42.93M outstanding, down from the 12.1% reported in its January 2026 13G/A. A large holder roughly halved its position during the drawdown, and that supply has now been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since the selling already happened. It is filed because it describes who still holds the stock into the print.
findings.independence: The Stock Titan headline 'BlackRock amended passive stake, voting power over 2.57M shares' (via https://www.rava.com/noticias?ticker=VITL_US, 10/27). The January 12.1% figure is from an ownership aggregator (https://blarkad.com/ticker/VITL/ownership).

outside_window.finding: Securities class action over the Feb 26, 2026 miss (ERP implementation), plus Bronstein, Gewirtz & Grossman 'investigation' releases on Oct 25 and 27. Litigation resolves long after the window.
Butter business wind-down by the end of FY2026; its exit costs ($7.8M in Q2 COGS) are added back to adjusted EBITDA. The financial effect completes in Q4 and after.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the skew (+4.0 vol points, downside paid) and the -4.5% 20-day drift, so the negative findings are partly priced. A 25.7%-of-float short that is still building argues against them, which is why p_up is 45 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 and core table (crowded short against a negative; negative agreeing with the skew): guidance/price-assumption finding -3.0 -> -2.0, pastured-promotion finding -1.0 -> -0.7; p_up 44 -> 45.

Lesson 6 (bar disputed, $182.3M against $199.8M): findings that depend on the bar capped small; velocity/distribution +1.0 -> +0.7, analyst-cut finding -0.5 -> -0.3; Cal-Maine read-through left at -0.5 (already small).
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the money funds slowed capex and operating losses with no ramp corroborated, and no covenant or going-concern flag was found, so it is near zero; -0.5 -> -0.3.
Lesson 5 (proxy): USDA wholesale is macro-to-company, but the company's own guide names category price as its condition, so it is kept as the largest finding, sized for magnitude uncertainty.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage) not applicable: 10 analysts. Lesson 2: no one-offs filed as findings; butter exit costs put in outside_window.
